title: feat!: consume the declarative index, drop the pkg_id requirement
body:
Teaches soar to install from the declarative, hash-pinned index that sbuilder produces, and removes the assumption that every package carries a `pkg_id`.

Needs pkgforge/sbuilder#16 and pkgforge/soarpkgs#964.

## Reading the new index

Published as `{format, packages}`, so a client can tell an index it cannot read from one that merely lacks a field. Anything without a `format` is treated as the older format, and existing repositories keep working untouched.

Packages declare their contents rather than having them guessed. `files` says what comes out of the artifact and where it lands:

```json
"files": [
  {"source": "fd-v10.4.2-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/fd",   "to": "bin/fd"},
  {"source": "fd-v10.4.2-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/fd.1", "to": "share/man/man1/fd.1"}
]
```

`to` is a path inside the package directory, so where a file lands says what it is. `bin/` is a command, `share/man/` a manual page, `share/*-completion*/` a completion. An empty `source` means the artifact is itself the file, which is how a bare binary or an AppImage says so, and `alias` lists other paths resolving to the same file, which is how `dunst` exposes `dunstctl` and `dunstify`.

The layout is built in a staging directory and swapped in at the end, so a source that fails to resolve never leaves a package with its binary deleted. If nothing resolves, the artifact is left as it is rather than installing an empty package. Anything unlisted is pruned, which is how READMEs and changelogs stop being installed.

## Linking beyond `bin`

Manual pages and completions only mean anything where the system looks for them, so they are linked out of the package: man pages beside the bin directory, completions into the per-shell directories, for the shells in `completions = [...]`, defaulting to those whose directory already exists. A destination holding something soar does not own is left alone, and removal takes back only links that resolve into the package being removed.

`soar health` gains a MANPATH row, shown once a package has installed a manual page. Worth knowing why: man-db discards everything it would derive when `MANPATH` is set explicitly, which distributions do, so pages can be installed correctly and still be invisible.

## pkg_id is optional

A repository whose names are already unique no longer has to invent ids, so `pkg_id` is nullable throughout and nothing fabricates one. Variants are selected by family instead: the query syntax is `family/name`, and `name#pkg_id` still works but warns.

One migration per database. The installed-package table gains `pkg_family`, the metadata table gains `files` and drops three columns nothing read, and both relax their `pkg_id` columns by rebuilding, since SQLite cannot drop NOT NULL in place. The metadata table also gains a `COALESCE(pkg_id, '')` unique index, because SQLite treats NULLs as distinct and the plain index would have allowed a fresh duplicate row on every sync.

Downgrading refuses rather than deleting installed rows that have no id. The metadata cache, being regenerable, just clears.

## Version ordering

Comparison is segment-wise: a version splits into runs of digits and runs of non-digits, and matching runs compare numerically. This fixes `10` sorting below `9` and `1.10` below `1.9`.

Semver is deliberately not used. Most published versions carry a rebuild revision as `-N`, which semver reads as a prerelease and ranks *below* the plain version, the opposite of what it means here, and plenty of real versions are not valid semver at all. Two commit hashes compare equal, so an arbitrary hash cannot read as an upgrade.

## Several versions are not several packages

A repository publishes every version it knows. Installing, running or listing a package by name means the newest, and `@version` picks another and pins it against `update`.

Previously any two candidates were treated as ambiguous, the CLI re-resolved the chosen one *by name*, got the same ambiguity back, and exited silently. That affected `install`, `run`, and 8 packages in soarpkgs. The chosen package is now used directly. `list` and `search` show one row per package with the other versions named, `18.18.1 (18.17.1)`, and `query` orders them newest first.

## Identity is repository, family, name and version

Everything that decides "is this the same package" now uses the whole identity. Previously the repository was missing from it, so installing the same name from a second repository did nothing, both variants stayed linked, and two repositories shipping byte-identical builds shared one directory, meaning removal of either destroyed the other's files. Package directories are now named `<name>-<version>-<hash>`, readable at a glance and unique per install.

`run` caches per exact package too, and reuses that cache: previously it re-downloaded every time, because it looked for the artifact at a path the layout step had pruned.

## Fixes found while testing this

- Archives are identified by content rather than declared type, so a bare `.gz` is no longer treated as a tarball
- Binaries resolve by full path before falling back to the file name, which stops an ARM binary being installed on x86_64
- Read-only directories from an archive no longer break extraction, layout or removal
- Removal is ownership-based, so it catches aliases and leaves other people's files alone, and a missing desktop directory no longer abandons it half-done
- Installed packages are matched by name rather than id, which was breaking upgrades of anything installed earlier

## Testing

All 140 non-AppImage packages in soarpkgs install and are verified against what their recipe declares, every path, alias and bin link: 140 passing, 0 failing. Separately `sync`, `list`, `search`, `query`, `install`, `info`, `run`, `download`, `update`, `remove`, `use`, `json2db` and `apply` are exercised end to end against a local index, including pinning, aliases and multi-version packages.

  * Added manual-page health reporting and improved package caching and execution.

title: fix(security): validate provides names to block path traversal
body:
Untrusted `provides` metadata was joined onto bin/install dirs verbatim, allowing arbitrary file deletion on remove and symlink planting on install. Validate names as single path components at import, and add ownership/containment checks at the remove and create sites.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Security & Reliability**
  * Strengthened safeguards for package-provided binary symlinks during installation and removal.
  * Added validation to reject unsafe provide names/targets (e.g., path traversal/absolute paths), with warnings when skipped.
  * Prevented unrelated files or symlinks from being overwritten or removed.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved cleanup to remove only symlinks that are owned by an installation, avoiding incorrect filesystem changes.

* **Tests**
  * Added unit test coverage for safe-path validation and provide symlink behavior.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

soar install --no-verify 'https://beeper-desktop.download.beeper.com/builds/Beeper-4.2.892-x86_64.AppImage'

title: soar update downgrades nightly neovim
body:
### Problem

`soar update` downgrades neovim from latest nightly to latest stable. When _nightly_ is explicitly requested in the TOML file.

### Steps to reproduce

Add this to `.config/soar/packages.toml`:

```toml
neovim = {
  github = "neovim/neovim",
  asset_pattern = "nvim-linux-x86_64.appimage",
  version = "nightly"
}
```

Then, run `soar apply` to install the latest nightly release of neovim.

Now, when running `soar update` neovim is downgraded to 11.6 and is modified `packages.toml` to fix the version to 11.6.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * New comprehensive operations module: install, remove, update, sync, apply diffs, search, list, run, and switch variants.
  * Improved install/update flow: URL/GitHub support, signature and checksum verification, concurrent/locked installations, and desktop integration.
  * Health checks: detect and remove broken packages and symlinks.
  * Rich progress/event notifications and detailed operation reports.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: feat(crates): add soar-events for frontend-agnostic event reporting
body:
Introduces the soar-events crate with a typed event system that decouples operation progress reporting from any specific frontend, enabling both CLI and GUI consumers.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Introduced a structured event model for operation lifecycles and logging.
  * Added flexible event sinks for emitting, collecting, and no-op handling.

* **Chores**
  * Added a new workspace crate to host the event infrastructure and made it available to the workspace.
  * Exposed event types and handles for consumption by other components.

title: Optional PkgForge backend for Penguins-Eggs (external adapter, no core changes) + Using PkgForge as a build/cache backend for Penguins-Eggs ISOs (external adapter)

labels.name: p3
labels.description: Low Priority (Maybe a while before it gets done/fixed)

body:
![file_00000000392871f8a131f5afd13adb90.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65d43ee9-3199-4030-afdd-b2f278924760)



[ Hello 👋

This issue proposes an *optional*, *external* integration between
Penguins-Eggs and PkgForge, implemented as a small adapter repo.
No core Penguins-Eggs code would be modified unless explicitly agreed.

### Summary
The idea is to allow Penguins-Eggs to **consume PkgForge-built artifacts**
as a package backend, alongside existing apt/apk/etc workflows.

Penguins-Eggs would remain fully independent and distro-focused;
PkgForge would simply act as an optional build + cache source.

### What this enables
- Reproducible ISO builds
- Reduced reliance on host distro repos
- Cleaner Alpine / non-Debian workflows
- Artifact caching and reuse
- Experimental distro-agnostic Eggs images

### What this does NOT do
- No repo merge
- No rewrite of Eggs internals
- No replacement of existing package managers
- No new mandatory dependency

### Proposed approach
- External adapter repo (`pkgforge-eggs`)
- Optional `pkgforge` backend selected via CLI
- Declarative manifest shared between projects
- Eggs remains authoritative over snapshot + ISO logic

### Status
This is currently a design + PoC proposal.
Feedback on scope and boundaries is welcome before any implementation.

Thanks for your time, and happy to adapt this to Eggs’ preferred workflow. ]

ChatGPT Chat Link : [ https://chatgpt.com/share/6983fc51-dbfc-8012-9a6c-d861f2750639 ]

Initial Inquiry : [ Could you assist with integrating, wrapping, merging & collaboration between Penguins-Eggs & PkgForge, please & thanks in advance.

https://github.com/pieroproietti/penguins-eggs

https://github.com/pieroproietti/penguins-packs

https://github.com/pieroproietti/fresh-eggs

https://github.com/pieroproietti/penguins-eggs-ppa

https://github.com/pieroproietti/penguins-alpine

https://github.com/pieroproietti/penguins-bootloaders

https://github.com/pieroproietti/eggsmaker

https://github.com/pieroproietti/pengui

https://github.com/pieroproietti/basket

https://github.com/pieroproietti/easy-menu-system

https://github.com/pkgforge

https://github.com/pkgforge/soarpkgs

https://github.com/pkgforge/devscripts

https://github.com/pkgforge/pkgs.pkgforge.dev

https://github.com/pkgforge/bin

https://github.com/pkgforge/aeris

https://github.com/pkgforge/soar

https://github.com/pkgforge/nix-appimage

https://github.com/pkgforge/sbuilder-go

https://github.com/pkgforge/sbuilder

https://github.com/pkgforge/squishy-rs

https://github.com/pkgforge/bincache

https://github.com/pkgforge/pkgcache

https://github.com/pkgforge/build-system

https://github.com/pkgforge/store.pkgforge.dev ]

Initial Response :

[ Oh this is a very good pairing. Penguins-Eggs and PkgForge actually complement each other almost suspiciously well 🐧🥚⚒️
I’ll break this down in a way that’s practical, realistic, and collaboration-friendly—not a big-bang merge that nobody wants to maintain.


---

Big picture: what this collaboration should be

Penguins-Eggs = system snapshot + live ISO + distro crafting

PkgForge = universal package production, caching, and distribution

Together, they can form a full lifecycle:

> Build system → package artifacts → cache/store → OS snapshot → ISO/image → redistribution



Think of Eggs as “what the system becomes”
Think of PkgForge as “how software gets built, cached, and shipped”


---

1. Conceptual integration map

Penguins-Eggs side (what Eggs already does well)

Component	Role

penguins-eggs	Snapshot → ISO
penguins-packs	Package grouping
fresh-eggs	Minimal base seeds
eggsmaker	Build orchestration
penguins-alpine	Non-Debian proof
basket	Package sets
pengui	UI frontend
bootloaders, easy-menu-system	Boot UX


PkgForge side (what it adds)

Component	Role

soar / soarpkgs	Universal package format
sbuilder(-go)	Reproducible builders
bincache / pkgcache	Artifact caching
store.pkgforge.dev	Distribution layer
nix-appimage	Cross-distro app builds
squishy-rs	Compression / FS tooling
aeris	Infra glue



---

2. Recommended integration strategy (no monorepo!)

❌ Don’t

Hard-merge repos

Rewrite Eggs around PkgForge

Force one build system onto the other


✅ Do

Layered integration

Optional backends

Shared schemas + conventions

Cross-project tooling



---

3. Concrete integration points (the juicy part)

A. PkgForge as an optional package backend for Eggs

Add a new Eggs concept:

eggs package-backend:
  - apt
  - apk
  - pacman
  - pkgforge (NEW)

What this enables:

Eggs ISOs built entirely from pkgforge artifacts

Mixed sources (base OS + pkgforge apps)

Zero reliance on host distro repos


Implementation

Thin adapter in penguins-eggs

Calls:

pkgforge/bin

soar install

pkgcache pull



No deep coupling required.


---

B. Eggs → PkgForge build pipeline

Eggs already knows:

Exact package set

Versions

Architecture

Kernel + init + boot config


That’s gold.

New workflow

eggs produce manifest
↓
PkgForge sbuilder
↓
soar package set
↓
bincache/store
↓
Eggs ISO build

Artifacts become:

Reusable

Cacheable

Shareable across distros


This turns Eggs from “snapshot tool” into a reproducible OS factory.


---

C. penguins-packs ↔ soarpkgs

This is a near-perfect match.

Penguins-Packs	PkgForge

Logical app groups	Soar package collections
Role-based installs	Declarative manifests
Desktop flavors	App bundles


Action

Define a shared YAML/JSON schema

Auto-generate:

penguins-packs from soarpkgs

soarpkgs from penguins-packs



This avoids duplication and keeps both ecosystems in sync.


---

D. Eggs + squishy-rs + store.pkgforge.dev

Eggs outputs:

SquashFS

ISOs

Rootfs trees


PkgForge offers:

Optimized compression

Artifact storage

CDN distribution


Result

Eggs ISOs published via store.pkgforge.dev

Delta updates for Eggs remasters

Versioned OS images


That’s huge for bandwidth and CI.


---

4. Alpine + non-Debian future

penguins-alpine + pkgforge/soar is where this gets spicy 🌶️

Alpine base

PkgForge apps

Eggs snapshot

Zero distro lock-in


You end up with:

> A distro-agnostic OS builder



This positions Eggs way beyond Debian tooling.


---

5. Collaboration model (this part matters)

Shared repos (new, small, neutral)

Suggested:

pkgforge-eggs-specs/
pkgforge-eggs-adapter/
eggs-pkgforge-manifests/

These should:

Be tiny

Be well-documented

Contain schemas + glue only


Maintainer boundaries

Eggs remains Eggs

PkgForge remains PkgForge

Integration lives between them


This avoids burnout and political friction.


---

6. Suggested phased roadmap

Phase 1 (low risk, fast win)

Eggs → pkgforge binary cache

Manual integration

Proof-of-concept ISO


Phase 2

Package backend abstraction

Auto-generated manifests

CI builds using sbuilder-go


Phase 3

Store publishing

Delta ISOs

UI support in pengui



---

7. What I can help you do next

If you want, I can:

Draft exact repo structure for the adapter

Write a PkgForge ↔ Eggs manifest spec

Sketch CLI commands (eggs pkgforge enable)

Prepare a maintainer-friendly pitch for both sides

Identify which repos should never be touched


Just tell me what you want to tackle first—and whether you want this framed as an experiment, addon, or long-term alliance.

This is one of the cleanest ecosystem fits I’ve seen in a while 👌 ]

title: Add an option for the shell script installer to place soar in `/usr/local/bin`

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### Problem

It would make it easier to install soar in /usr/local/bin without downloading it and copying it.

### Expected behavior

It would just give the option to install soar in `/usr/local/bin` instead of `~/.local/bin`

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Install/update packages from GitHub/GitLab releases; derive versions (incl. version_command), select assets via patterns, and update package targets from release assets.
  * New config options: github, gitlab, asset_pattern, include_prerelease, tag_pattern, version_command.

* **Refactor**
  * Unified URL/GitHub/GitLab package status and update flow; installations can propagate version changes back to packages.toml.

* **Improvements**
  * Normalize versions (strip leading "v") and refine package ID derivation for registry paths.

* **Style/Tests**

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Explicit binary mappings for package symlinks.
  * Package hooks: post-download, post-extract, post-install, and pre-remove (now run during install and before removal).
  * Build steps with dependency checks and optional sandboxed execution.
  * Package sandbox configuration for filesystem/network restrictions.
  * Archive options: nested-extract and extract-root.

* **Bug Fix / UX**
  * Progress display omits total when unknown, showing only current bytes.

### Problem

This is more of a feature that would be in the long term like probably at least 2 or more years from now. If you plan on supporting macos, only support Apple Silicon since macos intel is on life support right now and all intel macs will soon no longer have any updates whats so ever.

### Expected behavior

Feature Requests don't really need this part, this part is for bug reports.

title: Installer doesn't select the executable from archive unless name matches
body:
### Problem

When the executable file in the archive doesn't match exactly to the package name, it fails to install the package.

### Steps to reproduce

Add to `packages.toml`
```toml
trenchbroom = { url = "https://github.com/TrenchBroom/TrenchBroom/releases/download/v2025.3/TrenchBroom-Linux-x86_64-v2025.3-Release.zip" }
```

and `soar apply`

Since the file in the archive is named `TrenchBroom.AppImage`, it fails.
Naming package as `TrenchBroom.AppImage` doesn't work either since it's normalized to lowercase.

### Expected behavior

The installer should first check whether an executable with the **exact package name** exists.
If not, it should compare against **normalized filenames** and use a match if found.
If neither succeeds, it should **recursively search for other executable files** within the package directory.

Executable discovery should prioritize the following directories, in order:
1. `bin/`
2. `usr/bin/`
3. `usr/local/bin/`

### Soar version (soar -V)

0.9.1

### Operating system (if issue is related to OS)

_No response_

### Installation

_No response_

title: Support updates for remote package installations

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### Problem

Currently, the remote packages can't be updated automatically and the version needs to be set manually.

### Expected behavior

`soar` should handle updating remote package installations too.
- For AppImages supporting `zsync`, it'd be ideal to integrate `appimagetool`.
- For other packages, we should ideally allow user to specify how to fetch the latest package version (?) so it can work for any package regardless of the source.

body:
Currently partially fixes #128, where running `soar apply --prune` cleans up package of different version from what's listed under the toml. However, it doesn't clean it up under `soar clean`. Not sure why as pinning is already switched to false.

title: soar does not update the local version until you prune and reinstall
body:
### Problem

If you have a package without a specified version, and then you specify the version in the packages.toml later, it doesn't apply the version to `soar list-installed`. You have to comment the package, `soar apply --prune` it and then uncomment and `soar apply` to get the version to display properly in `soar list-installed`

### Steps to reproduce

have something along the lines of

```toml
[packages]
texlab = { url = "https://github.com/latex-lsp/texlab/releases/download/v5.24.0/texlab-x86_64-linux.tar.gz" }
```

`soar apply`

and then change the packages.toml to specify version:

```toml
[packages]
texlab = { version = "5.24.0", url = "https://github.com/latex-lsp/texlab/releases/download/v5.24.0/texlab-x86_64-linux.tar.gz" }
```

`soar apply` doesn't do anything, you'd have to comment the package, `soar apply --prune`, uncomment the package, and then `soar apply` to make it show version under `soar list-installed` 

### Expected behavior

I expected the package to have version attached to it after adding the version without this comment uncomment shenanigans

### Soar version (soar -V)

soar-cli 0.9.0

### Operating system (if issue is related to OS)

_No response_

### Installation

soar is bootstrapped to be installed from soar itself with 
`soar = { pkg_id = "github.com.pkgforge.soar.glibc-v4", repo = "bincache" }`

title: Nvidia driver not found in Runimage! (blender)
body:
### Problem

Hello, I'm playing around with soar.. I installed blender , and while launching I get a pop up saying "Nvidia driver not found in Runimage!" .Blender works, but without cuda or optix support. I'm on debian trixie, and I'm running the open-nvidia driver from nvidia cuda repository.. I didn't find any documentation regarding nvidia driver and soar online ..

Maybe I'm missing something very basic, like I should use the nvidia drivers provided by debian, OR nvidia is not supported at all 

Or, just like the  debian deb blender: is not compiled with cuda-optix support - for what I know, only on few distros, like cachyos, or endeavour os, alt linux the repo for blender works with cuda and optix.. On debian we should either use the binary from blender website, or flatpak..

### Steps to reproduce

soar defconfig --external (just in case)
soar install blender

### Expected behavior

Blender works with cuda and optix support, and possibly an updated version , like 5

### Soar version (soar -V)

soar-cli 0.9.0

### Operating system (if issue is related to OS)

Debian

### Installation

wget -qO- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pkgforge/soar/main/install.sh" | sh

title: Refactor Soar into Multiple Crates for Better Maintainability

labels.name: p1
labels.description: High Priority (Needs to be done/fixed at earliest convenience)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
This issue tracks the refactoring of the `soar`  codebase into multiple, well-defined crates to improve maintainability, modularity, and development workflow. This modular approach will enable better separation of concerns, easier testing, and allow for individual crate versioning.

## Goals

- Improved Maintainability: Separate concerns into focused, single-responsibility crates
- Better Testing: Enable isolated unit testing for individual components
- Modularity: Allow external projects to consume specific soar functionality
- Development Velocity: Enable parallel development on different components
- Code Reusability: Make soar components available as libraries for other projects
- Cleaner Dependencies: Reduce compilation times by having focused dependency trees

## Proposed Crate Structure
- [x] soar-core (refactor & cleanup)
- [x] soar-cli (refactor & cleanup)
- [x] soar-config - Configuration management
- [x] soar-dl - Merge from https://github.com/pkgforge/soar-dl for downloads
- [x] soar-package - Package format handling
- [x] soar-db - Database and package tracking
- [x] soar-registry - Repository interactions
- [x] soar-utils - Shared utilities for soar modules

## Testing Strategy

- Unit Tests: Each crate will have comprehensive unit tests
- Integration Tests: Cross-crate functionality testing
- Workspace Tests: Full system integration testing
- CI/CD: Separate testing pipelines for individual crates
- Benchmarks: Performance testing for critical paths

title: Soar 0.8.0 seems to be broken
body:
### Problem

An attempt to install any package results in:

```
Fetching metadata from https://meta.pkgforge.dev/external/pkgforge-cargo/x86_64-Linux.sdb.zstd
Fetching public key from https://meta.pkgforge.dev/pkgcache/minisign.pub
Fetching metadata from https://meta.pkgforge.dev/external/pkgforge-go/x86_64-Linux.sdb.zstd

[pkgcache] Repository synced
[pkgforge-cargo] Repository synced
[pkgforge-go] Repository synced
[ERROR] SQLite database error: table packages has no column named install_patterns
```

### Steps to reproduce

```
podman run -it --rm fedora /bin/sh -c 'cd /root && (curl -fsSL https://soar.qaidvoid.dev/install.sh | SOAR_VERSION=0.8.0 sh ) && ./.local/bin/soar install bottom && ./.local/bin/soar info'
```

0.7.0 works fine.

### Expected behavior

Packages should have been installed :)

### Soar version (soar -V)

soar-cli 0.8.0

### Operating system (if issue is related to OS)

Fedora 42

### Installation

`curl -fsSL https://soar.qaidvoid.dev/install.sh`

title: Add creating portable cache directory (`XDG_CACHE_HOME`)
body:
Introduced in uruntime since v0.4.4 release:
https://github.com/VHSgunzo/uruntime/releases/tag/v0.4.4

For other AppImages on older or different runtime, it would just be an unused directory, so it wouldn't harm anything.

Option would be included in `--portable` & new `--portable-cache`.

title: `--force` install even if checksum fails

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### Problem

When using AM packages, the checksum may not be updated because the checksum sis computed against the up-to-date package served by the external resource (e.g. the github repo of the software) while the soar's package metadata are updated only once in a while.

For instance `soar install aichat` right now fails because of the checksum mismatch.

### Expected behavior

Have an option to bypass the checksum check

labels.name: p1
labels.description: High Priority (Needs to be done/fixed at earliest convenience)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### Problem

Currently, there's no hardcoded list of repos to host matching, so soar simply enables all repos on a host regardless if the repos even exist for them

### Expected behavior

After https://github.com/pkgforge/soar/pull/67 is merged, there will be a repo -- host mapping.
And soar should enable repos conditionally based on this information.
This information would be updated/changed per release.

If soar is run on a host where there are no repos, it should exit with a message like:
`Our official repositories do not support x86_64-freebsd, please create a discussion or self-host your own`
It shouldn't enable any repos.

body:
Currently, soar will assume file exist if `file.sig` exist, this leads to weird errors and incomplete installs.
Soar should explictly check for existence of all `file` counterparts for each and every `file.sig` , and if and only if, both exist, the sign verification should continue, otherwise it should be silently skipped (or say failed to verify signature for file X (missing file))

title: Make (Most) Configuration possible using only ENV Variables

labels.name: p2
labels.description: Medium Priority (Needs to be done/fixed within 3 Weeks or less)

body:
As per: https://github.com/blue-build/modules/blob/soar-module/modules/soar/soar.sh

We need to allow users to configure most of the config via env variables directly.

- Config File path
Currently, allows `--config | -c` to specify a configuration file
Maybe, `SOAR_CONFIG_PATH` or something else

Similarly, 
```env
$ soar env
[NOTE]: These values are not configurable via environment variables. They are derived from the config file or defaults.
SOAR_CONFIG=/home/Ajam/.config/soar/config.toml
SOAR_BIN=/home/Ajam/.local/share/soar/bin
SOAR_DB=/home/Ajam/.local/share/soar/db
SOAR_CACHE=/home/Ajam/.local/share/soar/cache
SOAR_PACKAGE=/home/Ajam/.local/share/soar/packages
SOAR_REPOSITORIES=/home/Ajam/.local/share/soar/repos
```

We can make these configurable, by appending `_PATH` to these,
```env
SOAR_CONFIG_PATH=/some/custom/path
SOAR_BIN_PATH=/some/custom/path
SOAR_DB_PATH=/some/custom/path
SOAR_CACHE_PATH=/some/custom/path
SOAR_PACKAGE_PATH=/some/custom/path
SOAR_REPOSITORIES_PATH=/some/custom/path
```

And also some global (not just per repo) ones like:
```env 
DESKTOP_INTEGRATION=false #disables desktop integration for all repos globally
SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION=false #disables sign verification for all repos globally
SYNC_INTERVAL=12h #sets/overrides sync interval for all repos to 12hr
```

soar should check for these env vars every time it's run, if these aren't found or set to empty, then we should use the default path/file etc

title: -c flag does not change root_path in soar configuration
body:
### Problem

I noticed that when using the -c flag to specify a different configuration file, the root_path does not change as expected. Here are the details:

Configuration File (config.toml):
```
$ soar config
default_profile = "default"

[[repositories]]
name = "bincache"
url = "https://meta.pkgforge.dev/bincache/x86_64-Linux.sdb.zstd"
desktop_integration = false
pubkey = "https://meta.pkgforge.dev/bincache/minisign.pub"
signature_verification = true
sync_interval = "3h"

[[repositories]]
name = "pkgcache"
url = "https://meta.pkgforge.dev/pkgcache/x86_64-Linux.sdb.zstd"
desktop_integration = true
pubkey = "https://meta.pkgforge.dev/pkgcache/minisign.pub"
signature_verification = true
sync_interval = "3h"

[profile.default]
root_path = "/data/.local/share/soar"
```

```
$ soar env
[NOTE]: These values are not configurable via environment variables. They are derived from the config file or defaults.
SOAR_CONFIG=/home/ubuntu/.config/soar/config.toml
SOAR_BIN=/data/.local/share/soar/bin
SOAR_DB=/data/.local/share/soar/db
SOAR_CACHE=/data/.local/share/soar/cache
SOAR_PACKAGE=/data/.local/share/soar/packages
SOAR_REPOSITORIES=/data/.local/share/soar/repos
```

After moving the configuration file to a new location:
`$ mv ~/.config/soar/config.toml /data/.config/soar/`

Using the -c flag to view environment variables:
```
$ soar -c /data/.config/soar/config.toml env
[NOTE]: These values are not configurable via environment variables. They are derived from the config file or defaults.
SOAR_CONFIG=/data/.config/soar/config.toml
SOAR_BIN=/home/ubuntu/.local/share/soar/bin
SOAR_DB=/home/ubuntu/.local/share/soar/db
SOAR_CACHE=/home/ubuntu/.local/share/soar/cache
SOAR_PACKAGE=/home/ubuntu/.local/share/soar/packages
SOAR_REPOSITORIES=/home/ubuntu/.local/share/soar/repos
```



### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a configuration file with a specific root_path under [profile.default].
2. Run soar env to observe the environment variables.
3. Move the configuration file to a new location.
4. Run soar -c <path/to/new/config.toml> env and observe that SOAR_CONFIG changes but root_path and all dependent paths do not update.

### Expected behavior

When specifying a configuration file using the -c flag, it should allow the configuration file’s parameters—including root_path—to update accordingly.

### Soar version (soar -V)

soar-cli 0.5.14

labels.description: Low Priority (Maybe a while before it gets done/fixed)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
Homebrew offers a shell integration: https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-command-not-found
We should add this:

```bash
$ fastfetch
The program 'fastfetch' is currently not installed. You can install it by typing:

 * soar add "fastfetch#github.com.fastfetch-cli.fastfetch:bincache"
 (i) Notes:
    Built From Source (Latest Git HEAD). Check/Report @ https://github.com/fastfetch-cli/fastfetch
    This version contains a limited set of features due to static linking
    Please use the version from pkgcache if all features are needed

 * soar add "fastfetch#sharun.wrappe.stable.fastfetch:pkgcache"
 (i) Notes:
    Built Using Sharun [Stable]. Check/Report @ https://github.com/VHSgunzo/sharun
    Learn more @ https://docs.pkgforge.dev/formats/packages/archive
    [PORTABLE] (Works on AnyLinux)
    [NO_DESKTOP_INTEGRATION] (Does not need desktop integration)
    This version was repacked from official Deb & contains the most features
```

We already have `provides`, and we also need to parse both actual bin_name + symlink & then show all `pkg_id` with notes that have this in their `provides`


I found https://github.com/metafates/brewer which does this using some fancy rust crates like [nucleo](https://github.com/helix-editor/nucleo) along with embedding [skim](https://github.com/lotabout/skim)

title: Enable/Fix Verbose for core options

labels.name: p3
labels.description: Low Priority (Maybe a while before it gets done/fixed)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### Problem

The `--verbose` flag needs to work for at least the core cmds, currently it is a guessing game when using some of the options as to what exactly is happening
- For devs/maintainers, `--verbose` should be a way to diagnose & debug bugs/problems etc or just to get a better insight at lower level
- For users, `--verbose` should be a way to provide additional information when reporting a bug/issue
- Further, `--verbose` can also entirely replace `--debug` (--debug could be repurposed to `--verbose` + rusts trace)

### Expected behavior


- `soar add`
- [ ] Should show the metadata or sqlite query + returned table
- [ ]  Should show either `ghcr_blob`, or `ghcr_pkg` or `download_url` i.e whatever is being used to download the pkg & from where
- [ ] Should show the http requests (see soar dl below) & response (like brew)
- [ ] Should show the filesystem changes (currently it shows the final binaries and symlinks, but adding a few echo statements through the process would be more helpful)

- `soar del`
- [ ]  Should show pkg_name, pkg_id, description, version & notes for the pkg that needs to be removed (We have multiple versions of same pkg as well as unrelated pkg that have same name, if we show the basic info, it will prevent accidentally deleting/removing unintended pkgs)
- [ ]  Should print/show removed binaries (including symlink), similar to when using soar add
- [ ]  Should show reclaimed size
- [ ]  Unrelated, but soar del by default should prompt as it is destructive action, it shouldn't work non-interactively unless using `--yes`

- `soar dl`
- [ ]  Should show redirect location (like wget without -q) for the full chain until download starts
- [ ] Should show both Client's & Server's HTTP Headers (like httpie or curl -I) for the full chain until download starts

title: Intuitive and consistent soar CLI

labels.name: p3
labels.description: Low Priority (Maybe a while before it gets done/fixed)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
Hi, you are doing very good job :)

I was playing with soar and found some issues in CLI format. Here is my experience.

When I run `soar i krita` then this is displayed:
```
Multiple packages found for krita
[1] krita#gitlab.com.krita.krita.next-2025-03-22:pkgcache
[2] krita#gitlab.com.krita.krita.stable-5.2.9:pkgcache
[3] krita#runimage.alpine.krita-5.2.9:pkgcache
```

Okay... I installed the 1. by typing "1" and ENTER. It was installed successfully.

Then I wanted to install another (stable) version.

I tried `soar i krita` again...

But I could not install it:
```
[WARN] krita is already installed - skipping
No packages to install
```

Okay, but this message does not answer to me:
a) Which one exactly is installed?
b) How to specify  the exact version for the installation process?
c) Why there is not interactive picker anymore to install another one if there was previously?

Then I tried to specify full name which was presented by `soar i krita` before:
```
soar i krita#gitlab.com.krita.krita.stable-5.2.9:pkgcache
[ERROR] Package krita#gitlab.com.krita.krita.stable-5.2.9:pkgcache not found
No packages to install
```

I entered the exact full name which I choosed before and it does not work now?

Okay, maybe I need to omit the pkgcache part:
```
soar i krita#gitlab.com.krita.krita.stable-5.2.9
[ERROR] Package krita#gitlab.com.krita.krita.stable-5.2.9 not found
No packages to install
```

Nothing... 

Maybe omit the version?
```
soar i krita#gitlab.com.krita.krita.stable
```

Now it worked.

a) Why it does not work with full name if that is what `soar i krita` gave in the first install?
b) Why it does not work with version in the name?

Then I learned I can specify `soar i krita#all` and `soar i #something`

a) But why to use some magic `all` string in the location of package ID to get package options?
b) And why `soar i #something` installs ALL (typically huge amount of packages) and not display options?

I found it little bit not intuitive and it could be polished to be intuitive and consistent :)

### Expected behavior

Be more intuitive and consistent. Instead of wild syntax use well defined syntax and flags.

labels.name: p3

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
We now have https://docs.pkgforge.dev/repositories/external/cargo-bins, around ~ 3000 new pkgs
However, these are `tar.gz` and require:

1. Select a pkg, example `television`
```bash
PKG_NAME="television"
```
2. Download to temp location
```bash
soar dl "${PKG_NAME}" -o "./pkg.archive"
```
3. List files in the archive & copy
```bash
$ tar -tzf "./pkg.archive"
tv
#Notice that the file inside the archive is not exactly named same, so have to account for that
#If single file, then simply rename
#If multiple files, then prompt user to select the default bin, rename it and then copy, the other remaining bins should be copied-as-is
```

Relevant code: https://github.com/cargo-bins/cargo-quickinstall/blob/main/cargo-quickinstall/src/lib.rs

In the future more formats could be supported, for now `tar`, `tar.gz` & `tar.xz` are a must as these are the most common

title: Add a way to install only main binary/package (Needed files)

labels.name: p3
labels.description: Low Priority (Maybe a while before it gets done/fixed)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
Currently, there's no way to specify that soar install only the main binary/package

For instance: 
1. Install a minimal package
```bash
$ soar add "whoami#git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc"
[1/1] whoami#git.busybox.net.busybox.sta [━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━] 17.88 MiB/s    11.23 MiB/11.23 MiB
* whoami#git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc
  Built From Source (Latest Git HEAD). Check/Report @ https://git.busybox.net/busybox
  This is the standalone version i.e all applets were built individually
  Statically Linked on Debian (GLIBC)

Installed 1/1 packages
```

2. Find the size of the main binary
```bash
$ du -sh ~/.local/share/soar/packages/whoami-git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc-4bXEiXWyXgL9/whoami
844K    /home/runner/.local/share/soar/packages/whoami-git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc-4bXEiXWyXgL9/whoami
```

3. Find the size of the entire package
```bash
$ du -sh ~/.local/share/soar/packages/whoami-git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc-4bXEiXWyXgL9/*
32K     /home/runner/.local/share/soar/packages/whoami-git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc-4bXEiXWyXgL9/CHECKSUM
20K     /home/runner/.local/share/soar/packages/whoami-git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc-4bXEiXWyXgL9/LICENSE
40K     /home/runner/.local/share/soar/packages/whoami-git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc-4bXEiXWyXgL9/SBUILD
844K    /home/runner/.local/share/soar/packages/whoami-git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc-4bXEiXWyXgL9/whoami
12K     /home/runner/.local/share/soar/packages/whoami-git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc-4bXEiXWyXgL9/whoami.json
11M     /home/runner/.local/share/soar/packages/whoami-git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc-4bXEiXWyXgL9/whoami.log
40K     /home/runner/.local/share/soar/packages/whoami-git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc-4bXEiXWyXgL9/whoami.png
4.0K    /home/runner/.local/share/soar/packages/whoami-git.busybox.net.busybox.standalone.glibc-4bXEiXWyXgL9/whoami.version
```

Soar installed 11 MB of stuff that could have been skipped.

---
### Proposals
- [x] `--binary-only`
This could also be called `--bare` or something else
This would use `ghcr_blob` to download the main package, however to not break signing etc,
we can keep the existing logic but include only `pkg_name` + `pkg_name.sig` (sig would be removed after verification)

For `static` this would work out of the box, for other formats that need desktop integration, we can introduce
- [ ] `--minimal`
This would install the main pkg + icons/desktop files and nthg else

We can fetch logs etc on demand if local file doesn't exist 

> [!NOTE]
> It is better to reserve `--needed` as it is already used by pacman and implies: Install only if not already installed
---

Where would this be useful?
For starters, would save lots of bandwidth & storage for power users (who read manuals)
And on containers where storage is crucial, adding these option would make soar ideal choice rather than hackish script in bash that do the same thing
